title: How do standard time series forecasting benchmarks translate to finance? A broad study of risk adjusted performance
abstract: arXiv:2603.01820v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Forecasting financial asset returns is challenging due to low signal-to-noise ratios, non-stationarity and heavy-tailed distributions. We benchmark 16 deep learning architectures for time series forecasting, including Transformers, State Space Models (SSMs), xLSTMs and recurrent hybrids, on a 15-year daily futures dataset using an end-to-end volatility-targeted Sharpe ratio optimisation task. Our results challenge prevailing assumptions in the literature. Several widely used 'state-of-the-art' architectures, including generic Transformers and SSMs, underperformed a simple AR(1) benchmark in a realistic financial forecasting task. The strongest results came from comparatively simple hybrid approaches using recurrent structures: a Variable Selection Network combined with an LSTM achieved the highest Sharpe ratio, while xLSTM showed the greatest robustness to transaction costs. translated_title: 标准时间序列预测基准如何迁移到金融领域？一项关于风险调整绩效的广泛研究
translated_abstract: 由于信噪比低、非平稳性和重尾分布，预测金融资产收益率极具挑战性。我们在一个15年的期货日线数据集上，通过端到端的波动率目标夏普比率优化任务，对16种深度学习时间序列预测架构进行了基准测试，其中包括Transformer、状态空间模型（SSM）、xLSTM和循环混合模型。我们的结果挑战了文献中的主流假设：若干被广泛使用的“最先进”架构，包括通用的Transformer和SSM，在现实的金融预测任务中表现不及简单的AR(1)基准模型。表现最好的是采用循环结构的相对简单的混合方法：变量选择网络与LSTM的组合取得了最高的夏普比率，而xLSTM则展现出对交易成本最强的鲁棒性。这些发现表明，在标准时间序列基准上取得的成功并不能直接转化为金融领域的成功。
tldr: 该研究在15年期货数据上通过波动率目标夏普比率优化任务对16种深度学习预测架构进行基准测试，发现通用Transformer和SSM等主流“最先进”模型表现不及简单的AR(1)基准，而基于循环结构的简单混合模型（变量选择网络+LSTM夏普比率最高、xLSTM对交易成本最鲁棒）表现最佳，表明标准时间序列基准上的成功难以直接迁移到金融预测任务。
en_tdlr: Benchmarking 16 deep learning architectures on a 15-year futures dataset with an end-to-end volatility-targeted Sharpe ratio optimization task, the study finds that generic Transformers and SSMs underperform a simple AR(1) baseline, while simple recurrent hybrids perform best—a Variable Selection Network combined with an LSTM achieves the highest Sharpe ratio and xLSTM shows the greatest robustness to transaction costs—suggesting that success on standard time-series benchmarks does not translate to finance.
